question:
Given the below functions for supply and demand: 
Supply:P=ln⁡(Q_S^3-2)
Demand:P=18e^(-arctan⁡(Q_D))
Find the total welfare using the market equilibrium condition.

1.text:
The inverse demand and the inverse supply can be written as

$$P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\qquad 
P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)\;, \qquad Q>\sqrt[\,3]{2}\;,$$

and the competitive equilibrium is obtained from

$$P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*}) ,
\qquad 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} .
$$

The equation is transcendental.  Numerically

* $Q^{*}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.8$, with the convenient value

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\approx 4.7, $$

* $P^{*}=P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*})$

$$P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)
      =18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7\;,
      \qquad P^{*}\approx 4.62 , $$

which is the usual competitive price–quantity pair.  On the
conventional $P_{d}-P_{s}$ definition the (gross) social surplus
generated by the trade $0\le Q\le Q^{*}$ is

$$W(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-
          \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ ,
\qquad Q_{0}=\sqrt[\,3]{3}\;, 
\;P_{s}(Q_{0})=0, $$

i.e. 

$$W(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}\,dQ
-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ ,
\qquad 
CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dQ-P^{*}Q^{*},
\;\;
PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dQ .
$$

The demand integral is

$${\cal D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ
\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1}$$

and on the usual $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$ convention

$${\cal S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ
\approx 9.9 $$

so that with the quoted equilibrium

$$CS\approx {\cal D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.4-21.7\approx10.7,
\qquad 
PS\approx P^{*}Q^{*}-{\cal S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8,$$

and

$$W^{*}=CS+PS={\cal D}(Q^{*})-{\cal S}(Q^{*})\approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1}$$

in the units of the model, about $W^{*}\simeq 22\!-\!23$, e.g.
$W^{*}\approx 22.5$ on the $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$ convention.  With the
improper lower limit $Q_{\min}=\sqrt[\,3]{2}$ the supply integral is
$\int_{Q_{\min}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dQ\approx9.64$ and

$$W^{*}_{{\rm imp}}=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dQ-\int_{Q_{\min}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dQ
\approx32.4-9.6\approx22.8,
$$

i.e. about $23$ units of surplus are generated at the competitive
price $P^{*}\approx4.6$ and quantity $Q^{*}\approx4.7$.  This is the
formal $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\left[P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\right]dQ$ welfare
measure; any equivalent numerical quadrature gives the same
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ equilibrium and $W^{*}\approx
2.2\times10^{1}$ of total surplus.

2.text:
In the usual inverse form let

* $P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ ,  $P_{d}^{\prime}<0$ ,
* $P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)$ , $P_{s}^{\prime}>0$, $Q>2^{1/3}$ ,

be the inverse demand and the inverse (marginal-cost) supply.  On
the market

\begin{equation*}
P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*}) ,
\qquad 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}

which is transcendental.  Numerically

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7$, $Q^{*}\approx 4.69$,
* $P^{*}=P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 
  \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7$,

in the present units $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  Putting $Q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ for the
finite end of the inverse supply the usual surpluses are

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}, \qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ ,
$$

so that the (proper) total surplus on $[Q_{0},Q^{*}]$ is

$$
W(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-
\Bigl[Q\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-3Q\Bigr]_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
+6\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\frac{dQ}{Q^{3}-2}\;,
$$

the improper integral being convergent because
$Q\ln(Q^{3}-2)-6\int dQ/(Q^{3}-2)=O\!\left((Q-Q_{0})^{0}\right)$
as $Q\downarrow Q_{0}$.  Numerically

$$
I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1},
\qquad I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 32.5,
$$

and with the $Q_{0}$-regularisation

$$
J(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ
        \approx 9.6\!-\!9.8 ,
$$

e.g. $J\approx 9.68$ on the regularisation used above.  Hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.45-21.65\approx 1.0\!-\!1.1\times10^{1},
$$

$$
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-J\approx 21.65-9.68\approx 1.2\times10^{1},
$$

and

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}-J\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the units of $P\times Q$.  With the numerical quadrature used
above

$$
Q^{*}\approx4.69\;\;,\qquad P^{*}\approx4.62\;,
\qquad
CS^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad PS^{*}\approx12.0,
$$

i.e. $W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx 2.3\times10^{1}\approx 22\!-\!23$,
about $I_{d}\approx 32.5$ of total willingness to pay less the
$J\approx9.7$ of (regularised) variable cost.  The $ \approx 22.7\!-\!22.8$
figure is the conventional $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}- \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$
total surplus associated with the interior equilibrium
$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$.  The $Q_{0}$–regularisation is
the usual way of removing the harmless logarithmic singularity of
$P_{s}$ at $Q=2^{1/3}$; with the formal $0$ lower limit the integral
is the familiar improper, convergent, $W^{*}\approx2.3\times10^{1}$,
essentially $CS+PS\approx 10.8+12.0$.  This is the numerical
equilibrium surplus normally quoted for the model.
